chapters.text: Define the measurement before comparing the numbers. Here, the starting event is a request to change connectivity, before choosing the next topology. The ending event is when the endpoints can use the new path. Starting after schedule selection would answer a narrower question and exclude some preparation work.

The paper identifies five contributors: scheduler, control, switch, transceiver, and host. In a fully serial example, each waits for the previous stage, so their durations add. This makes a useful first budget, provided the start and end events include all of the required work.

Now shorten only the switching stage. The lightpath changes sooner, but the rest of the sequence remains. If receiver recovery or scheduling dominates, an impressive device improvement produces only a small improvement in usable-path readiness. This is why the smallest advertised component number is a poor summary of system performance.

A different design moves work off the critical path. It can select a predictable schedule in advance, distribute it before use, and coordinate local actions at an agreed time. Work is not eliminated simply because it is hidden. Its completion, timing, and validity must still be assured before the new connection is needed.

The actual delay follows the longest chain of dependencies that cannot overlap. Compare designs using that critical path and the same measurement boundaries. The animation illustrates relationships rather than a measured product. A complete evaluation must also say how synchronization, queues, unsuccessful requests, and endpoint readiness are included.
